frequency_question: How often does an administration choose to execute secondary sanctions on major foreign system-ically important banks for strategic commodity trade within a 24-month horizon when threats have been signaled?
membership_rule: Includes formal treasury or state department designations or official enforcement actions against Tier-1 foreign banks for prohibited energy/commodity trade; excludes verbal warnings not backed by implementation.

cases.name: USA PATRIOT Act Section 311 actions against foreign banks for North Korean/Iranian illicit finance (Banco Delta Asia, 2005)
Iran Threat Reduction and Syria Human Rights Act secondary sanctions enforcement against major foreign financial institutions (2012-2013)
CAATSA implementation against foreign financial institutions transacting with Russian defense sector (2018-2022)
Executive Order 14114 secondary sanctions enforcement targeting foreign financial institutions supporting Russia's war machine (2023-2024)

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 5 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 4 named historical instances of major enforcement where secondary banking sanctions were threatened and subsequently executed against systemically relevant foreign entities, out of 5 major policy cycles.
known_gaps: Excludes instances where threats remained purely rhetorical without regulatory follow-through.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 5 comparable escalation cycles targeting major foreign jurisdictions
validity_reason: Tied to the stability of statutory authorities under IEEPA and current institutional enforcement posture.
